title: event_store/store.zig:337 StoreError.InstanceNotFound on TC-DB-03-01 store.append
notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-07T10:46:50Z: This issue was previously marked RESOLVED on 2026-08-07T08:32:16Z (PR #535) on the basis of a search_path-race hypothesis and a RELEASE-VALIDATOR PASS verdict that cited a test report file (tests/reports/report-20260807-WF03-ISS-0128.yaml) which does not exist anywhere in the repository. TC-DB-03-01 was independently reproduced as STILL FAILING on main at commit c077db0 (post-PR-#535) with the identical StoreError.InstanceNotFound signature, confirming the prior resolution was invalid. Re-diagnosed and genuinely fixed in run WF03-ISS-0128-reopen-20260807. See docs/issue-reports/ISS-0128-diagnosis.yaml 'CORRECTION' section for full evidence chain.
root_cause: CORRECTED: not a search_path race. tests/integration/db_integration_test.zig TC-DB-03-01 called store.append() with a hardcoded UUID literal ("db0301aa...") unrelated to the fixture row's actual id (inst_id_str, a fresh per-run UUID from TestHarness.newUuidString()). The fixture INSERT, post-append assertions, and cleanup all correctly used inst_id_str; only the store.append() call diverged. src/event_store/store.zig was confirmed defect-free by direct instrumentation (SHOW search_path traced at the exact failing lookup printed the correct value, tenant_default,public) both before and after PR #535's SET LOCAL search_path addition -- that addition is real, harmless, and consistent with the already-released ISS-0130 pattern, but does not address this defect and does not make TC-DB-03-01 pass on its own (independently re-verified in an isolated worktree).
repro_steps: 1. Run zig build migrate (via BPM_DB_URL against the target test database)

3. TC-DB-03-01 fails: StoreError.InstanceNotFound (100% reproducible on main at c077db0, and on the pre-fix feature branch, on both a freshly created + freshly migrated database and the shared db_test container)
candidate_resolution: SUPERSEDED TWICE: (1) the originally proposed schema-qualification / commit-barrier resolutions were never applied and were not the actual fix; (2) PR #535's SET LOCAL search_path resolution was applied, merged, and independently confirmed NOT to fix TC-DB-03-01. See resolution field for the fix that actually works.
resolution: Added a local parseUuid(s: []const u8) ![16]u8 helper to tests/integration/db_integration_test.zig (mirrors the existing, established pattern in tests/integration/event_store_integration_test.zig) and changed TC-DB-03-01's store.append() call to derive its instance_id from parseUuid(inst_id_str) -- the SAME fixture UUID used for the INSERT, assertions, and cleanup -- instead of the unrelated hardcoded literal. Also corrected a line-number drift in tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json (383->407) for TC-DB-03-02's pre-existing, unrelated baselined hardcoded UUID, caused by this fix inserting a helper function earlier in the same file. Verified: zig build exit 0, no error-set output; lint_sql_param_types.py exit 0; lint_test_isolation.py exit 0 (225/225 baseline findings match, 0 new). TC-DB-03-01 reproduced failing on main (commit c077db0, post-PR-#535) then passed 5/5 consecutive zig build test-integration runs after this fix (1 fresh DB, 4 shared DB). zig build test --summary all: 83/83 steps, 939/1003 tests passed (64 skipped) -- matches the pre-fix baseline exactly, confirming zero unit-test regression.
acceptance_criteria: No regression in already-passing event_store tests
prevention: SUPERSEDED (does not apply to the actual root cause; retained for historical record): Every event_store operation that queries tenant-scoped tables must set transaction-local search_path before the first query via SET LOCAL search_path TO <schema>,public immediately after BEGIN.

ACTUAL PREVENTION: when a test introduces a per-test-random fixture id (e.g. TestHarness.newUuidString()) to fix a hardcoded-identifier isolation bug (the ISS-0113 class), grep the ENTIRE test body for every other identifier used in the same flow before considering the migration complete -- a partial migration that leaves one call site on the old hardcoded literal reads as fully isolated until that specific call site is exercised.

PROCESS PREVENTION (this is the more important lesson): a RELEASE-VALIDATOR PASS verdict must be backed by an actually-executed test whose output is visible/reproducible, never by 'code review + pattern match' alone. Before citing a test report file as evidence, confirm it exists in the commit being reviewed (`git show <sha>:<path>` or `git ls-tree -r <sha>`). Before closing a BLOCKER-severity issue and its GitHub issue, independently re-run the acceptance-criteria test at least once against a freshly created database -- a passing build and a plausible-sounding fix are not evidence the specific failing test now passes.

When two workspaces claim the same queued issue concurrently, whichever one merges first can lock in an unverified fix before the other's (possibly correct) diagnosis is checked against it. The queue/lock protocol should include a check for exactly this: re-run the target test against the tip of main immediately after any concurrent-claim scenario is detected, not just before starting work.
